page.layout: One printed page. Running head at top: "Cap.42." left and "AVGVSTINVS" right. Main text in one full-width column of roman type. Centred ornamental band, then centred chapter heading "CAP. XLII." with subtitle in italic-free roman. Below: a paragraph opening with a large woodcut initial "R" in an ornamental frame, set in italic. Then a paragraph beginning with a numbered marker "2" followed by italic "Origeniani.)" which stands as a paragraph opener in the text. No marginal notes.

main_text.p: etiam numero, non tantùm genere & speciè ὁμοούσιον, id est, essentiam diuinam docere, constituere & defendere: in ea verò essentia tres ὑποστάσεις id est, personas & subsistentias agnoscere, vt veteres verterunt. Itaque neque deos numero multos facimus, cùm non separemus diuinam illam naturam: neque personas tollimus, quia quenque, id est Patrem, Filium, & Spiritum sanctum in diuina essentia propriam personam habere demonstrauimus. Vt autem hæc commodissimè docerentur, voces ὑπόστασις & ὁμοούσιος sunt à Patribus receptæ, vt ait Socrat. lib. 3. cap. 7. Ruffin. libr. 1. cap. 29. ac ὑπόστασις quidem vocabulũ aduersus Arianos: ὁμοούσιος autem aduersus Sabellianos: vt omnis in disputando ambiguitas tolleretur.
main_text.head: CAP. XLII. Origeniani vnde dicti. Erroris autem eorum caput vnum recensetur.
main_text.p: Rigeniani¹ à quodam Origene dicti sunt, non ab illo, qui fere omnibus notus est, sed ab alio nescio quo, de quo vel sectatoribus eius Epiphanius loquens, Origeniani, inquit, sunt cuiusdam Origenis discipuli, turpis autem sunt operationis. Ipsi sunt nefanda facientes, sua corpora corruptioni tradentes.
2. Origeniani.) Pauca sunt omnino quæ de hac hærefi dici queant, cùm præter vnum Epiphanium nemo fide dignorum scriptorum scripserit.

page.notes: The chapter number XLII is printed as a Roman numeral. Greek words in the first paragraph are transcribed as printed in the scan; several Greek forms (ὁμοούσιον, ὑποστάσεις, ὑπόστασις, ὁμοούσιος) are rendered approximately and should be checked against the scan. The woodcut initial "R" is uncertain and marked by the first word "Rigeniani", which is probably "Origeniani" with an ornamental initial; the reading is doubtful. The footnote marker "2." and "Origeniani.)" are printed in the text block. The text is cut off at the bottom of the page at "pserit," which is the printed word of the sentence continuing on the next page. The text in this page's italic paragraph has uncertain letters, so that passage is provisional.
